resolutions: The admonitive is positive warning or advice, not negative mood, prohibition, or a separate imperative.
A nonpast admonitive uses the perfective stem even though its meaning is nonpast.
Class A marks admonitive tense with h, while Classes B, C, and D use their proper perfective zero realization.
Singular admonitives use ⎕-Ø and plural admonitives use t-in or t-ih; these are automatic number realizations.
Affirmative admonitions require mā; optional nēn strengthens them without changing their positive warning force.
A negative admonition uses ah and obligatory mā nēn to cancel caution; it is not the Lesson 9 ca negative command.
Subject person gives direct admonition, indirect admonition, or admonitive exhortation without changing the construction into a command or wish.
The full Class A through D contrast paradigms come from the same canonical generator, not from copied tables.
Compressed table witnesses such as mahuetz preserve their source provenance but normalize to the separate grammatical words mā huetz.
Lesson 10 reuses Mood, Subject, Polarity, Particles, and the full paradigm; stem shape, affixes, boundaries, roles, and reading warnings remain application obligations or derived cues.
